I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrectly retained when following prefetches back to a parent object.

### Cause of the Issue
When evaluating a prefetch query for a related object manager (e.g. `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, or `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`), `get_prefetch_queryset` iterates through the fetched related instances (`rel_obj`) to automatically set the reverse/back-reference cache pointing back to the parent instance (`instance`). 

When nested prefetches were specified on the related queryset (e.g., `Prefetch("user", queryset=User.objects.only("kind"))`), evaluating `queryset` inside `get_prefetch_queryset` executed the nested prefetch queries first and populated `rel_obj` with the newly fetched nested object instance. However, immediately after `queryset` evaluated, `get_prefetch_queryset` unconditionally set `setattr(rel_obj, self.field.name, instance)` (or `set_cached_value`), overwriting the newly prefetched instance on `rel_obj` with the outer parent instance (which had deferred fields from the outer queryset).

### Solution
In `django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`, updated `get_prefetch_queryset` for `ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor` so that reverse back-reference instances are only cached on `rel_obj` if the relation field on `rel_obj` is not already cached by a nested prefetch query.
